subject: Databases
title: Database System Concepts
subtitle: Relational Models, SQL & Transaction ACID
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth & S. Sudarshan

pages.title: The Relational Model & Relational Algebra
bulletPoints: Relational model fundamentals: Relations (tables), tuples (rows), attributes (columns), and atomic domains.
Integrity constraints: Entity integrity (primary key uniqueness), referential integrity (foreign keys), domain constraints.
Relational algebra fundamental operators: Select (sigma), Project (pi), Union (cup), Set Difference (-), Cartesian Product (times).
Additional operators: Natural Join (bowtie), Theta Join, Rename (rho), and Division.

pages.title: SQL Fundamentals & Complex Queries
bulletPoints: Data Definition Language (DDL): CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, DROP TABLE, primary/foreign key definitions, constraints.
Data Manipulation Language (DML): SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE syntax and execution semantics.
Aggregation and Grouping: GROUP BY, HAVING, and aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX).
Nested Subqueries: Correlated vs uncorrelated subqueries, IN, EXISTS, ALL, ANY, and Common Table Expressions (WITH clauses).

pages.title: Entity-Relationship (E-R) Modeling
bulletPoints: E-R Modeling concepts: Entity sets, attributes (simple, composite, multivalued, derived), and relationship sets.
Mapping cardinalities: One-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, many-to-many relationship constraints.
Participation constraints: Total participation (double lines) vs partial participation.
Specialization and Generalization: Top-down specialization, bottom-up generalization, and aggregation abstractions.

pages.title: Relational Database Design & Normalization
bulletPoints: Pitfalls in relational design: Data redundancy, update anomalies, insertion anomalies, and deletion anomalies.
Functional Dependencies (FDs): Alpha -> Beta assertions; Armstrong's Axioms (reflexivity, augmentation, transitivity).
Attribute closure algorithm: Computing alpha+ to find candidate keys and verify dependency preservation.
Canonical cover: Minimal set of functional dependencies equivalent to a given set of FDs.

pages.title: Normal Forms: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, and BCNF
bulletPoints: First Normal Form (1NF): All attribute domains must contain only atomic (indivisible) values.
Second Normal Form (2NF): 1NF plus no non-prime attribute is partially dependent on any candidate key.
Third Normal Form (3NF): 2NF plus no transitive dependencies (if X -> Y, X is superkey or Y is prime attribute).
Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF): For every non-trivial dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey; lossless-join decompositions.

pages.title: Storage Structure & File Organization
bulletPoints: Physical storage hierarchy: Cache, main memory, flash memory SSDs, magnetic hard disks, tape libraries.
File organization: Heap file organization, sequential file organization, and multitable clustering.
Record allocation in blocks: Fixed-length records vs variable-length records with slotted-page block architecture.
Buffer management: Managing the buffer pool, dirty page writes, and pin/unpin page reference counters.

pages.title: Indexing & B+ Tree Data Structures
bulletPoints: Index classifications: Primary (clustering) index vs Secondary (non-clustering) index; Dense index vs Sparse index.
B+ Tree structure: Balanced search tree where all data records reside at leaf nodes linked in a doubly linked list.
B+ Tree search: O(log_B N) root-to-leaf traversal; node splitting upon insertion overflow and node borrowing upon deletion underflow.
Multilevel indexing and index sequential access method (ISAM) architecture.

pages.title: Hashing Techniques & Dynamic Hashing
bulletPoints: Static hashing: Hash functions mapping search keys to bucket addresses; collision resolution via overflow chaining.
Hash index vs B+ Tree index: Hash index provides O(1) exact match lookup but cannot support range queries.
Dynamic hashing: Extendible hashing and Linear hashing adjusting bucket allocations gracefully as data volume grows.
Bitmap indexing: Space-efficient encoding for low-cardinality attributes (e.g. gender, status, country).

pages.title: Query Processing: Parsing & Translation
bulletPoints: Steps in query processing: Parsing and translation -> Optimization -> Evaluation engine.
Relational algebra equivalence rules: Commutativity and associativity of joins, projection and selection pushdown.
Evaluating relational operators: Implementation algorithms for Selection (file scan vs index scan).
Sorting algorithms: External merge-sort algorithm for datasets exceeding available RAM buffer size.

pages.title: Join Algorithms: Nested-Loop, Merge & Hash
bulletPoints: Block Nested-Loop Join: Iterating outer blocks and inner blocks; cost = B_r + (B_r / (M - 2)) * B_s block I/Os.
Indexed Nested-Loop Join: Using index on inner relation to lookup matching tuples in O(log N).
Sort-Merge Join: Sorting both relations on join attributes and merging sorted streams in linear time.
Hash Join: Partitioning both relations using hash function on join key and probing matching hash buckets.

pages.title: Query Optimization & Cost Estimation
bulletPoints: Cost-based query optimization: Estimating execution costs using catalog statistics (table cardinality, block counts).
Selectivity estimation: Estimating result size using uniform distribution assumptions, histograms, and sampling.
Join order optimization: Dynamic programming over left-deep join trees to find the minimum cost plan.
Heuristic optimization: Pushing selections down, pushing projections down, and performing most restrictive joins first.

pages.title: Transaction Concept & ACID Properties
bulletPoints: Transaction definition: A unit of program execution that accesses and possibly updates various data items.
Atomicity: Either all operations of the transaction are completed successfully, or none are reflected in the database.
Consistency: Execution of a transaction in isolation preserves the consistency invariants of the database.
Isolation: Transactions execute concurrently without witnessing the uncommitted intermediate states of other transactions.
Durability: Once a transaction commits, its modifications persist permanently even upon sudden system crash.

pages.title: Concurrency Control & Serializability
bulletPoints: Transaction states: Active, Partially Committed, Failed, Aborted, Committed.
Conflict Serializability: A schedule is conflict serializable if it is conflict equivalent to a serial schedule.
Precedence Graphs (Serialization Graphs): Directed graph where cycles indicate non-serializable concurrent schedules.
View Serializability: Weaker serializability condition accounting for blind writes.

pages.title: Lock-Based Concurrency: Two-Phase Locking
bulletPoints: Lock modes: Shared lock (S) for reading and Exclusive lock (X) for writing; lock compatibility matrix.
Two-Phase Locking (2PL) protocol: Growing phase (acquiring locks) and Shrinking phase (releasing locks).
Strict 2PL: Holding all exclusive locks until transaction commit/abort, preventing cascading rollbacks.
Rigorous 2PL: Holding all shared and exclusive locks until transaction completion, guaranteeing serializability.

pages.title: Deadlock Handling in Databases
bulletPoints: Deadlock conditions: Two or more transactions waiting for locks held by each other in a cyclic dependency.
Wait-For Graph (WFG): Directed graph of transactions; cycles indicate deadlocks; background deadlock detection threads.
Deadlock prevention schemes: Wait-Die scheme (non-preemptive) and Wound-Wait scheme (preemptive) based on timestamps.
Deadlock recovery: Victim selection, transaction rollback (total vs partial to savepoint), and starvation prevention.

pages.title: Timestamp-Based & Validation Protocols
bulletPoints: Timestamp-Ordering protocol: Ordering transaction execution according to monotonically increasing timestamps TS(T).
Read and write timestamp tracking: R-timestamp(Q) and W-timestamp(Q) for each data item Q.
Thomas' Write Rule: Obsolete write rule optimizing timestamp ordering by ignoring out-of-order writes.
Optimistic concurrency control (Validation-based): Read phase, Validation phase (checking conflicts), Write phase.

pages.title: Recovery Systems & ARIES Algorithm
bulletPoints: Failure classifications: Transaction failure, System crash (power loss), Disk failure (media corruption).
Write-Ahead Log (WAL) records: <T, X, V1, V2> storing transaction ID, data item, old value, and new value.
Checkpointing: Fuzzy checkpoints writing dirty buffer pages to disk and recording active transaction tables.
ARIES recovery process: Analysis pass (reconstructing state), Redo pass (repeating history), Undo pass (rolling back uncommitted work).

pages.title: Distributed Databases & 2PC Protocol
bulletPoints: Distributed database architecture: Data fragmentation (horizontal and vertical), replication, and allocation.
Two-Phase Commit (2PC) protocol: Phase 1 (Prepare / Voting) and Phase 2 (Global Commit / Abort).
Coordinator failure modes: Blocking problem when coordinator crashes after participants vote YES.
Three-Phase Commit (3PC): Adding a pre-commit phase to eliminate blocking under non-network-partitioning assumptions.

pages.title: NoSQL Databases & The CAP Theorem
bulletPoints: The CAP Theorem (Brewer's Conjecture): A distributed data store can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance.
BASE philosophy: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventual consistency.
NoSQL data models: Key-Value stores (Redis), Document stores (MongoDB), Wide-Column stores (Cassandra), Graph databases (Neo4j).
Consistent Hashing and tunable consistency levels (Quorum R + W > N) in Dynamo-style distributed systems.

pages.title: Data Warehousing & OLAP Cubes
bulletPoints: OLTP (Online Transaction Processing) vs OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) workloads.
Dimensional modeling: Star schema (central fact table surrounded by dimension tables) vs Snowflake schema.
Data warehouse architectures: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipelines and staging areas.
OLAP operations: Roll-up (aggregation), Drill-down (increasing detail), Slice and Dice, and Pivot.

pages.title: Object-Relational & JSON Databases
bulletPoints: Object-Relational Mapping (ORM): Impedance mismatch between relational tables and object-oriented memory models.
Complex data types: Nested relations, array attributes, and spatial data types (PostGIS).
JSON/BSON document storage: Storing semi-structured documents directly in relational columns (PostgreSQL JSONB).
GIN and GiST generalized search tree indexes for fast semi-structured document searching.

pages.title: Database Security & Access Control
bulletPoints: Authentication and authorization: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and discretionary access control (DAC).
SQL GRANT and REVOKE commands for table, column, and view permissions.
SQL Injection prevention: Parameterized queries, prepared statements, and input validation.
Encryption: Data at rest (transparent data encryption TDE) and Data in transit (TLS/SSL).

pages.title: Database Tuning & Performance Benchmarking
bulletPoints: Indexing strategies: Creating composite indexes, covering indexes, and avoiding index bloat.
Query plan analysis: Using EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE to identify sequential scans and costly joins.
Schema denormalization: Selectively introducing redundancy to eliminate expensive join operations on hot paths.
Standard benchmarks: TPC-C (OLTP transactional throughput) and TPC-H (OLAP analytical queries).

pages.title: Spatial & Temporal Databases
bulletPoints: Spatial data: Points, lines, polygons representing geographic and geometric information.
Spatial indexing: R-Trees (bounding boxes) and Quadtrees for multi-dimensional spatial range queries.
Temporal databases: Valid time (when fact is true in reality) and Transaction time (when fact was recorded in database).
Bitemporal tables: Tracking historical corporate changes and audits with temporal primary keys.

pages.title: Future Trends: Cloud-Native & NewSQL
bulletPoints: Disaggregated storage and compute: Amazon Aurora, Google Cloud Spanner, and Snowflake architectures.
NewSQL systems: Delivering horizontal distributed scalability while preserving strict ACID transactional semantics.
TrueTime API: Synchronized atomic clocks and GPS receivers providing global external consistency in Google Spanner.
Vector databases: Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) indexes (HNSW) powering large language model retrieval (RAG).
